subject: Private hosting: legal redlines and alternative to full escrow
messages:

To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Priv hosting — license scope & audit addendum (initial redlines)

Karthik / Redwood team,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal ran our standard hosting checklist against the MSA + Order Form and attached a set of redlines (GOH_MSAA_redlines.pdf). High-level asks from GreenOak: 1) a clear operator-access boundary for any private/VPC deployment, 2) a deterministic audit evidence path (we need to be able to demonstrate access and snapshots if we exercise host-proof), and 3) an escrow-like mechanism for continuity — our procurement team prefers an escrow deposit of runtime artifacts + sealed snapshot with an independent custodian.

We appreciate Redwood's typical witness/auditor approach but need specifics on what you can commit contractually. Please confirm whether you can:
- provide a sealed snapshot deposit model (custodian vs. trustee approach) or a functional alternative,
- constrain operator access to named roles + timeboxed sessions, and
- accept a 90-day evidence access window for audit triggers (we proposed this in redlines).

Can we get your legal view by EOD tomorrow? If useful, loop in whoever handles on-prem licensing and deployment evidence. We have a procurement call Thursday at 2pm PT and would like to present Redwood's proposed pathway.

Thanks,
Angela Ruiz
Senior Counsel, GreenOak Health
Angela.ruiz@greenoakhealth.com

Attachment: GOH_MSAA_redlines.pdf (PDF, 112KB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: lauren.bishop@redwood.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 3 Feb 2026 12:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Priv hosting — license scope & audit addendum (initial redlines)

Angela — thanks for the redlines and the clear asks. I reviewed the PDF with our solutions lead this morning and wanted to propose a pragmatic path so your procurement call has options. Summary attached: redline-summary.md (short bullets).

Two alternatives we can offer:
1) Witness-lite custody: Redwood deposits a sealed runtime snapshot with an independent custodian, plus a documented auditor-witness process to validate integrity when triggered. This avoids full-transfer escrow while meeting continuity needs.
2) Trustee escrow (custodial): full artifact escrow with a third-party trustee and a staged release process — takes longer and would be an add-on to the Order Form.

Operator access: we can contractually limit operator access via RBAC + ephemeral console sessions (justified and logged), and we can expand that with an explicit operator-access exhibit in the MSA.

We want to run these options past Legal — looping in Lauren to weigh in on exposure and acceptable contract language, and Neha to align on commercial implications. If we can agree on 1) an evidence access window (90 days), 2) a limitation on operator access (named roles + max session duration), and 3) indemnity guardrails for snapshot use, we can present a tidy compromise on Thursday.

Proposed next step: 30-min sync with procurement + Legal tomorrow or Wednesday to align language. Lauren / Neha, can you weigh in on the two options below and flag any absolute no-go items?

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com

Subject: RE: Priv hosting — license scope & audit addendum (initial redlines)

Folks — quick legal read. Attached are my notes: legal-comments-privdeploy.txt. Key points and suggested contract language/change requests: 

- License scope: do not expand runtime license beyond "customer-hosted runtime for Customer internal use". Add explicit prohibition on reuse/sublicense by any third-party without written consent.
- Operator access: accept named-role, just-in-time console sessions limited to 2 hours for remediation; require pre-approval for any live troubleshooting that exceeds 30 minutes and must be logged and notarized in audit trail.
- Evidence & snapshots: witness-lite deposit is acceptable if: snapshot is sealed with HSM-derived hash, custodian contract expressly restricts access to triggering events, and release requires multi-party signoff (Customer + Redwood + Trustee).
- Trustee escrow: OK only if commercial terms address verification fees and escrow termination triggers; procurement will need budget.
- Indemnity/data use: carve out forensic use only; Redwood must not use snapshot for training or benchmarking. Add explicit non-use clause with audit right.
- Time windows: 90-day evidence access window is reasonable; add a one-time 30-day extension option with joint approval.

Redlines I flagged as problematic: any clause that allows operator "broad" access or perpetual snapshot release without joint signoff. Also want contract language that limits obligation to provide access to the narrow set of artifacts necessary for continuity.

If GreenOak insists on custody (trustee escrow), we should ask for a scoped order form fee and an acceptance test for the snapshot release process.

Happy to join the procurement call Thursday. If we go with witness-lite, I can prepare an exhibit that captures the HSM/hash spec, custodian SLA, and the release authority matrix.

-Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.com

Attachment: legal-comments-privdeploy.txt (text, 9KB)

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: RE: Priv hosting — license scope & audit addendum (initial redlines)

Angela — appreciate the clear redlines and Lauren's rapid commentary. Based on Legal's guidance, Redwood can propose the following compromise for your procurement call Thursday: 

1) Offer: Witness-lite sealed snapshot + custodian model. Redwood will:
   - create a sealed runtime snapshot (hash signed by HSM),
   - deposit snapshot with an independent custodian under a tri-party agreement, and
   - define release only on a documented trigger (customer insolvency, cessation of service, or mutually agreed continuity event).

2) Operator access: Contractual limit to named roles; RBAC enforced; sessions are ephemeral, logged, and require pre-approval for remediation >30 minutes. Logs and session recordings will be part of the audit package.

3) Evidence access window: 90 days post-trigger, with a one-time 30-day extension if both parties agree. Any access requires trustee coordination and a signed use-limited agreement (forensic-only; no reuse for model training).

4) Commercials: Witness-lite custody is included in the proposed Order Form. Trustee escrow (full custody) is available as a paid add-on with acceptance testing; timeline for trustee escrow 6–8 weeks.

Next steps: 
- If this looks acceptable, I can table the witness-lite exhibit and a short tri-party template for Thursday.
- Lauren offered to draft the exhibit that contains HSM/hash spec and release matrix.
- If you want trustee escrow instead, Neha can follow up with commercial terms and a separate SOW.

Can we lock a 30-min call Thursday at 2pm PT to finalize which pathway procurement will present? If not, propose two time windows and we'll make it work.

Best regards,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
